statements.text: The score measures how much of the best documented setup the site has in place, weighted by the strength of the documentation. A documented practice counts whether or not the site has started on it. It is not a ranking prediction.
Just because a page meets these requirements doesn't mean that a page will be indexed; indexing isn't guaranteed.
Weights express the strength of the documentation, not ranking impact.

classes.assigned_when: It must be done this way or it does not work, is ignored, or the page or feature is ineligible. The source is an engine, or the standard that defines the mechanism itself (robots.txt, sitemaps, canonical links) stating that non-conforming input is ignored, dropped or invalid
classes.label: Mechanism

classes.assigned_when: The engine recommends it, or documents it as used by its ranking systems
classes.label: Recommended

classes.assigned_when: A web standard requires or recommends it, without a documented consequence for crawling, indexing or display
classes.label: Standard

classes.assigned_when: It is supported, optional, a policy choice or a house convention
classes.label: Informational

formulas: Achieved A = Σ (w_r × p_r / n_r) / Σ w_r over scored rules with at least one evaluated unit, where a unit is evaluated when it passes, fails or carries an opportunity; gate: indexing rules are excluded
Eligibility E = (|I| − |B|) / |I| where B = members of I failing at least one gate: indexing rule
Overall S = round_half_up(100 × E × A); round_half_up(a/b) = floor((2a + b) / (2b))
Category S_k = round_half_up(100 × A_k) with A restricted to the category's rules and no E factor

claims.claim: Titles must be about 60 characters
claims.evidence: "While there's no limit on how long a <title> element can be, the title link is truncated in Google Search results as needed"

claims.claim: Meta descriptions must be about 155 to 160 characters
claims.evidence: "There's no limit on how long a meta description can be"

claims.claim: A missing meta description is an error
claims.evidence: Snippets "are primarily created from the page content itself"; the scanner reports a missing description as an opportunity (SEO-META-02C), never as a failure

claims.claim: Every page needs exactly one H1
claims.evidence: Google: heading order doesn't matter for Search; the HTML Standard allows several top-level headings

claims.claim: Heading order affects Google rankings

claims.claim: Sitemap priority and changefreq matter
claims.evidence: Google ignores both; Bing says they "do not influence how your content is crawled or ranked"

claims.claim: A sitemap improves rankings
claims.evidence: Sitemaps help discovery and do not guarantee crawling or indexing

claims.claim: Submitting or listing a URL guarantees indexing
claims.evidence: Google does not guarantee it will crawl, index or serve a page, even one that follows Search Essentials

claims.claim: A perfect PageSpeed score is needed
claims.evidence: Good tool results don't guarantee top ranking; chasing a perfect score for SEO "may not be the best use of your time"

claims.claim: HTTPS gives a direct ranking boost
claims.evidence: A "very lightweight signal" in 2014; the current page experience documentation says aspects beyond Core Web Vitals "don't directly help" ranking

claims.claim: Duplicate content triggers a penalty
claims.evidence: Ordinary duplication is "not a violation of Google's spam policies"

claims.claim: nofollow links are never crawled
claims.evidence: Such links "will generally not be followed"; linked pages may still be crawled by other paths

claims.claim: Linking out to authoritative sites boosts rankings
claims.evidence: External links "can help establish trustworthiness (for example, citing your sources)"; no ranking gain is documented

claims.claim: E-E-A-T is a ranking factor
claims.evidence: "E-E-A-T itself isn't a specific ranking factor"

claims.claim: AI-generated content is automatically penalized
claims.evidence: Scaled content abuse applies "no matter how it's created"; using AI is not itself a violation

claims.claim: A .com outranks other TLDs
claims.evidence: TLD impact on Google performance: "No."

claims.claim: Keywords in the domain or URL rank pages
claims.evidence: Keywords in the domain or path "alone have hardly any effect beyond appearing in breadcrumbs"

claims.claim: Blocking GPTBot removes a site from ChatGPT search
claims.evidence: OAI-SearchBot governs ChatGPT search; "Each setting is independent of the others"

claims.claim: Blocking Google-Extended removes a site from Google Search
claims.evidence: Google-Extended "does not impact a site's inclusion in Google Search nor is it used as a ranking signal"

claims.claim: Bounce rate or analytics data are ranking factors
claims.evidence: No reviewed Google document names them

claims.claim: Buying ads improves organic rankings
claims.evidence: Participation in an advertising program "doesn't positively or negatively affect inclusion or ranking"

claims.claim: Third-party "authority" scores are engine metrics
claims.evidence: No engine publishes such scores; they are vendor constructs

not_scored.intro: Each row is a claim that circulates widely and is contradicted, dismissed or unsupported by the primary record. The scanner must never emit a fail for these, under any configuration, and must never recommend them. One carve-out: heading levels are scored by SEO-HDG-02 strictly as HTML Standard conformance (C3), and its reason must never connect heading order to Google. When the report touches one of these topics, it uses the stated verdict. A house convention that overlaps a myth (for example, a title-length hint) may exist only as a -HC info item, and its text must quote the source below.

recommendations.action: Write a short description specific to this page that states its most relevant facts; start with the home page and the most visited pages, and never reuse one description across pages.

citations.quote: If you don't have time to create a description for every single page, try to prioritize your content; at the very least, create a description for the critical URLs like your home page and popular pages.
citations.section: Create unique descriptions for each page on your site

citations.quote: create descriptions that accurately describe the specific page. Use site-level descriptions on the main home page or other aggregation pages, and use page-level descriptions everywhere else.
citations.section: Create unique descriptions for each page on your site

citations.quote: Snippets are primarily created from the page content itself.
A good meta description is short, unique to one particular page, and includes the most relevant points of the page.

recommendations.outcome: This follows a documented Google recommendation. Google publishes no ranking weight for it.
recommendations.reason: https://www.example.com/ has no meta description. Google asks that, at the very least, the critical URLs like the home page and popular pages have a description, and that page-level descriptions be used everywhere else. Snippets are primarily created from the page content itself, so nothing breaks without one.
verify: Re-run the scan after deploying the fix and compare the reports.
For a sample URL, use URL Inspection in Google Search Console to confirm how Google sees the page.
